Oliver —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers here and I attached a concise PDF (redwood_encryption_answers_v1.pdf) with specifics you can drop into your RFI spreadsheet. Quick bullets: 

- BYOK import: we accept PEM, PKCS#12 (RSA/ECC) wrapped keys. We recommend RSA-OAEP or AES-KW (RFC 3394) for transport wrapping. We perform server-side envelope wrapping using a hardware-backed master key.
- HSM support: Redwood integrates with cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and supports PKCS#11 and KMIP interfaces for private deployments. For Dedicated/VPC deployments we can place HSMs in-customer VPCs (subject to procurement/ops planning).
- Key rotation and zero-downtime: Customer can rotate CMKs at any time. We maintain key versioning and envelope-key mapping in the runtime so existing ciphertext decrypts against prior versions — typical rotations are zero-downtime for reads; re-encryption on write is configurable.
- TLS: we prefer TLS 1.3 with ECDHE (secp256r1/secp384r1) + AES-GCM / Chacha20-Poly1305; 1.2 is supported for legacy clients with strong cipher suites only. Mutual TLS is available for Private deployments.
- Audit logs: key import, key usage (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign), rotation events, and admin actions are logged. Default retention 90 days; we can stream to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, or Datadog).

I'll let Rishi add the technical appendix for HSM topology. If that works, Marissa can propose a short PoC plan. Happy to set a 60-min technical deep dive.

— Vivek

Oliver — adding the requested technical appendix inline for your security team (pulled from the PDF). If anything below needs extra detail we can include exact commands in the PoC repo.

----- Technical appendix (answer snippets) -----

1) BYOK import formats & example
- Supported formats: PEM (RSA/ECDSA private keys), PKCS#12 (.p12) with optional password.
- Recommended transport wrapping: RSA-OAEP with SHA-256, or AES Key Wrap (RFC 3394) for symmetric key blobs.
- Example (wrap with OpenSSL RSA-OAEP):
  openssl rsautl -encrypt -oaep -inkey redwood_wrap_pub.pem -in cmk_private.key -out cmk_private.key.enc
- Import API: POST /v1/kms/import-keys (multipart/form-data) with metadata: algorithm, key_usage, wrap_algorithm, origin=EXTERNAL.

2) HSM topology & integration
- Modes supported: 
  a) Redwood-managed cloud HSM (we provision and manage CloudHSM instances in your VPC for Dedicated customers).
  b) Customer-owned HSM (PKCS#11 or KMIP) integrated via a secure gateway — responsibility split documented in SOW.
- Interfaces: PKCS#11, KMIP, AWS CloudHSM SDK. We perform remote attestation of HSMs for managed installs and rotate attestation keys quarterly.
- Key export policy: HSM-protected keys never leave HSM in plaintext; exports are disabled for HSM-origin keys.

3) Rotation, caching, and zero-downtime
- Key versioning: every CMK rotation produces a new key version. Each ciphertext includes a version header; decryption checks version and uses the correct wrap key.
- Runtime caching: serving nodes cache envelope keys for performance. Cache TTL defaults to 5 minutes for hosted, configurable to 30s for stricter customers. Cache invalidation triggered on rotation or key disable events; we push invalidation via the control plane and fall back to synchronous KMS calls if needed.
- Re-encryption: optional background re-encrypt job to move old ciphertext to new key versions; recommended for long-lived objects.

4) TLS and cipher suites
- Default: TLS 1.3 with TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.
- Fallback: TLS 1.2 only with ECDHE_RSA + AES_256_GCM if client compatibility requires it (we block weak ciphers).
- Mutual TLS: supported on Dedicated/Private endpoints for ingress; we can enforce client certs and map them to RBAC principals.

5) Audit and evidence
- Logged events: key import, import validation result, key enable/disable, rotation, usage (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign), export attempts, admin key policy changes.
- Default retention: 90 days; configurable via Enterprise add-on to 365+ days. Logs can be exported in near real-time to S3, Splunk, or Datadog. Sample audit CSV attached (redwood_kms_audit_sample.csv).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and KMS architecture diagram provided in links.

Operational notes & constraints
- When using customer-provided HSMs inside a VPC we require a staging window (1–2 weeks) and a network design review.
- Key import requires an integrity check (SHA-256 fingerprint) and an HSM-wrapped import token for managed HSM flows.

Next steps
- We can produce exact OpenSSL / PKCS#11 example commands in the PoC repo.
- Marissa will send SOW/NDA and calendar invite for Thu 17 Jun technical deep dive.

If you want I can also record a short screencast of the import flow.

— Vivek
